title: Evidence for the cooking of fish 780,000 years ago at Gesher Benot Ya’aqov, Israel
version: Nature Ecology & Evolution 6 (2022), 2016–2028. Publisher record, ResearchGate full-article transcription and publisher supplementary PDF. Author contributions corrected in 2023 (10.1038/s41559-023-02270-y).
lineage: Publisher figures and supplement, and a ResearchGate transcription of the published PDF. The post-depositional alteration and heating comparisons are reported by the fish study; its hearth proxy uses burnt flint microartifacts from the earlier Gesher excavations.

passages.note: The study identifies eight tooth-rich Area B horizons in Layer II-6 with different taxa and skeletal elements from the Area A natural-death comparison.

passages.locator: Fig. 4, Extended Data Fig. 5 and Supplementary Text D
passages.note: X-ray diffraction compares changes in enameloid crystallite size and microstrain with experimental heating and fossil comparisons. Some Area B specimens resemble the moderately heated experimental group.

passages.locator: Fig. 5 and Supplementary Text E, Figs. 1–2
passages.note: Kernel density maps show spatial overlap of fish remains and burnt flint clusters. Supplementary Text E describes the excavation grid, the assignment of plotting coordinates and separate fish hotspot tests.

passages.quote: no traces of cooking apparatus have been preserved at the site
passages.note: The authors argue for cooking rather than simple direct burning of discarded fish. They suggest an earth oven as one possible explanation.
